text: The current inflationary environment is a global phenomenon.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Singapore Government has adopted a range of measures to mitigate the impact of inflation.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have undertaken several rounds of monetary policy tightening and rolled out three support packages last year, totalling more than $3.5 billion, to address cost-of-living concerns.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In addition, Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong has also announced several measures this year to support our businesses, including an extension of the enhancements to the Enterprise Financing Scheme to help enterprises access credit, as well as an extension of the Energy Efficiency Grant to encourage businesses to invest in raising their energy efficiency.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Minister of State Low Yen Ling will share more details in her speech.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Given that we are a small and open economy, we cannot be totally insulated from these global inflationary pressures.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For us to remain competitive, we must continue to improve efficiency and raise productivity.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: If we look beyond the near term, there are major structural shifts in our operating environment that will create both challenges and opportunities for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The multilateral open trading system is under pressure and geopolitical tensions are increasingly shaping countries' economic strategies.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These developments will undoubtedly have implications on the global economy as well as Singapore's economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: New technologies are disrupting industries and business models, such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) for example.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As AI technology improves and becomes integrated in more applications, such as ChatGPT, which many of us are familiar with and I hope none of us are using it to prepare our speeches.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These applications could take over tasks in areas such as marketing and sales, IT and engineering, and change the way we do business.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I agree with Mr Don Wee, that climate change is the defining challenge of our time.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The transition to net-zero emissions will be one of the deepest and broadest transformations to our economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It will affect almost every industry, every company, from energy to manufacturing, transport to financial services.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our local workforce is ageing and we are faced with the stark reality of a slowing local workforce growth.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: If we are to keep our economy vibrant, we must continue to deepen our skills and accommodate new arrivals to complement our local workforce, so that we can allow our companies to grow.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will require difficult trade-offs to be made carefully, not just at the company-level, but also as an economy and as a society.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: While these shifts may seem daunting, we are moving forward from a strong position, given our robust fundamentals.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These include our efficient infrastructure, extensive physical and trade connectivity, a highly-skilled workforce which we continuously invest in, and our nimble and enabling policy environment.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These were the same fundamentals that saw us through the COVID-19 pandemic and which demonstrated to our businesses and investors that Singapore is a reliable partner, even in a crisis.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We can, therefore, take heart that if we are willing to work hard and work together, we can turn challenges into opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Last year, I spoke about the Singapore Economy 2030 vision, in particular about our Manufacturing 2030 and Trade 2030 strategies.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Today, I will introduce our Services 2030 vision, and elaborate on what we are doing as part of our Enterprise 2030 strategy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: On Services 2030, our Services cluster encompasses very diverse sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It includes outward-oriented sectors such as Information and Communications, and Professional Services, as well as domestic-facing ones, such as the Retail Trade and F&B services.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It is also a very large cluster, accounting for around 70% of our Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our Services 2030 vision seeks to harness the growth opportunities in digitalisation and sustainability, and anchor Singapore as a leading, vibrant hub for businesses, lifestyle and tourism.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In particular, the Modern Services cluster comprises some of the fastest-growing sectors in our economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: A good example is the Professional Services sector within these Modern Services.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It is a diverse group too, including company headquarters, professional services firms providing consulting, legal and accounting services.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Together, they contribute to Singapore's vibrant business and innovative ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our Professional Services sector is well-positioned to seize opportunities for business growth driven by digitalisation, sustainability, emerging markets and new customer segments in Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Government will work with stakeholders to help Singaporeans upskill and reskill, so that they, too, can tap on opportunities and realise their career aspirations in this sector.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Minister of State Alvin Tan will elaborate on our strategies in this regard, including the Professional Services ITM 2025.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Professional Services ITM is one of the 23 ITMs that the Government introduced in partnership with the Future Economy Council Clusters, to support industry transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Several members, including Mr Pritam Singh during the Budget debate, asked about our ITMs.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The 23 ITM sectors have led the way in terms of economic growth and industry transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: However, the COVID-19 pandemic had inevitably affected the progress of some of them.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Across the 23 ITMs, from 2016 when they were introduced to 2021, their VA, in real terms, grew by 2.9% per annum.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This was marginally above the performance of the economy as a whole, which was at 2.8% per annum.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: However, if we only look at the period just prior to COVID-19, from 2016 to 2019, the VA in real terms for the 23 ITMs sector, grew by 3.5% per annum, which was a fair bit higher than the performance of the economy as a whole, averaging 3.1% per annum.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The ITM sectors, as a whole, also did better for productivity, which grew by 4% per annum for the period 2016 to 2021, compared to the overall economy at 3.5% per annum.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Close to 26,000 PMET jobs were created during this period, far exceeding the target of 12,000 jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: On the other hand, under the Precision Engineering ITM, we had set a nominal VA growth target of 8% and a job creation target of 3,000 PMET jobs by 2020.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Over the period 2016 to 2021, the sector exceeded its VA target and achieved growth of 11.2% per annum.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: But it did not do as well in job creation, creating over 2,000 PMET jobs, partly because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: While COVID-19 has disrupted the progress of our ITMs, we have since embarked on a refresh of the ITM strategies – the ITM 2025 refresh.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To take into account our experience during the pandemic and address emerging priorities, such as sustainability and the need for greater economic resilience.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We should allow some time for these strategies to take root, and then assess again the progress of the ITM 2025 strategies.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In essence, ITMs reflect the story of our economic development and constant transformation to respond to challenges and stay ahead of the curve.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ms Jessica Tan and Mr Saktiandi Supaat rightly pointed out that these same challenges can also create opportunities that businesses can capture.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: COVID-19 gave a decisive push for many businesses to adopt digital tools, such as digital shopfronts and e-payments.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Going forward, digitalisation will remain critical in helping companies raise productivity and optimise their operations, and to alleviate higher costs and manpower challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As supply chains increase in complexity and unpredictability, digital capabilities will also allow companies to have greater visibility of their operations and pre-empt bottlenecks.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: More importantly, digital technology can unlock companies' ability to innovate and develop new services and products.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We saw the sector take off during COVID-19, as people turned to seeing their doctors online instead of visiting the clinics physically.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Today, Singapore has a growing telehealth ecosystem, with several companies that have started to expand their operations overseas.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: One example is Doctor Anywhere, which was founded in 2017.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The homegrown company grew its user base in Singapore by three-fold and expanded to Malaysia and the Philippines in the midst of COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Today, it is present in six key Southeast Asian markets, and in time to come, I am sure Doctor Anywhere will be everywhere.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In the area of sustainability, investors and customers are raising their expectations.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This may be a challenge, but many Members also rightfully highlighted the opportunities this presents for our companies.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Having a clear sustainability strategy and statement will increasingly be an advantage when serving global markets, and companies need to urgently re-think how to transform their business models and operations to thrive in a low-carbon world.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: There are ready solutions, such as more energy-efficient equipment, for which Government funding support is available.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Koda, a leading Original Design Manufacturer of furniture, is a good example of a company that is transforming itself to compete in a low-carbon world.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The company has implemented a comprehensive environmental tracking and management system for its furniture manufacturing operations.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It is also developing a comprehensive sustainability strategy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Minister of State Alvin Tan will elaborate on how we are supporting our companies to seize opportunities in digitalisation and sustainability in his speech.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Even as we press on with the transformation of industries, we must continue to strengthen Singapore's position as a global hub for businesses, innovation, investors and talents.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This has allowed us to attract global companies and investors to invest in Singapore, creating opportunities and jobs, even in the depths of the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We must work even harder to secure Singapore's competitiveness as an investment location.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is crucial, as the international tax landscape is also going through a significant and fundamental change with the introduction of Base Erosion and Profit Shifting 2.0, or BEPS 2.0 in short.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Several Members rightly pointed out that Singapore will, indeed, be affected.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We need to carefully assess the impact of BEPS 2.0 on affected Multinational Enterprises, or MNEs, here, and on our overall competitiveness as a global business hub.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As Deputy Prime Minister Wong has said, we will also continue to monitor international developments and adjust our implementation timeline as needed.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Mr Sharael Taha asked about the use of non-tax incentives to enhance our competitiveness.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) has continuously sharpened our toolkit to ensure that Singapore remains competitive in attracting and retaining investments.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is in addition to its existing focus on productivity improvements, and continuing education and training.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I agree with Mr Sharael Taha on the importance of ensuring that projects supported by the NPF lead to real productivity improvements.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We currently fund a diverse portfolio of programmes and schemes under NPF, ranging from sector-specific ones like the Construction Productivity and Capability Fund (CPCF) under the Building and Construction Authority (BCA), to horizontal programmes, like the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These schemes have, thus far, achieved positive results.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: A 2016 study showed that the median firm saw an increase in revenue of 3.1% after adopting solutions under the scheme, compared to firms that had not adopted the solutions. iSPRINT has ceased in 2018, but SMEs can continue to tap on the SMEs Go Digital programme, which provides a range of support to meet businesses' digitalisation needs.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Apart from productivity indicators, each NPF project also has specific KPIs that they must meet, in areas like upskilling of individuals and development of industry platforms, such as centres of excellence – all of which contribute to productivity growth.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will continue to ensure that funds are used judiciously to support investment promotion, enhance our productivity and deliver tangible benefits to our businesses and workers.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will allow us to attract investments which are expected to generate significant economic contributions to Singapore over time.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Besides companies, we also want to attract high calibre investors who can strengthen our ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Such investors bring with them capital that support the growth of our local businesses and create good jobs for more Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: They also provide valuable networks to connect us to the region and beyond as well as contribute their entrepreneurial skills to our business ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Global Investor Programme (GIP) is one way through which we attract and anchor these investors in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The programme has delivered tangible outcomes for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To ensure that Singapore captures even more value from the capital, businesses and networks that the investors bring, the Economic Development Board will enhance the GIP by raising the investment quantum to ensure greater contributions from these investors and to direct more funds and resources into our local ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In addition, the scope of the GIP-select funds will be adjusted to capture more value from a wider pool of investors.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: EDB will share more details in due course.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To build a strong Singapore Economy 2030, we cannot just rely on foreign investments.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Nurturing a deep bench of local enterprises that are innovative, future-oriented and which can find success beyond Singapore shores is a key priority.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ms Janet Ang asked how MTI is assisting local companies to seize new opportunities and compete successfully in international markets.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: One way we do so is through our strong trade connectivity, leveraging on the network of 27 Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) that we have.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Such agreements help reduce uncertainties, risks and friction that businesses face when venturing into overseas markets.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For example, Prima Food's ready-to-cook products are now sold in over 40 markets, facilitated by preferential access through our FTAs.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Prima also exports products like wheat flour and premixes to Japan under the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), which provides tariff savings of about 20%.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are also making inroads in pioneering new agreements in emerging areas to create opportunities for our businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To date, we have signed four Digital Economy Agreements and concluded the first Green Economy Agreement with Australia last year.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Enterprise Singapore also has a range of schemes to help Singapore companies address common pain points and support them through the different stages of their internationalisation journey.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In 2022, we supported 2,000 enterprises to embark on internationalisation activities, which was 25% more than the year before.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To help companies break into new markets, we will make further enhancements to our existing programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For the Market Readiness Assistance scheme (MRA), we had in 2020 introduced a time-limited higher grant cap of $100,000 until 31 March 2023, which is next month.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I am heartened to hear from Ms Janet Ang of the value that the industry sees in the MRA.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ms He Ting Ru suggested having an Exim Bank for our local companies.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have indeed provided financing support to enterprises through various financing schemes to help them venture into overseas markets.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These include the Enterprise Financing Scheme or EFS-Trade Loan and EFS-Project Loan.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ten years ago, we also set up Clifford to provide financing for local companies doing infrastructural projects abroad.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Specific to green financing, we recently launched EFS-Green, in addition to MAS' green financing initiatives.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These may include costs arising from business advisory, product listing and marketing content development.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Beyond schemes and trade agreements, we have also facilitated partnerships between global companies and local enterprises to help local enterprises internationalise.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: One example is Singapore garment manufacturer Teo Garments and 3D apparel design solution provider Browzwear's partnership with Lidl & Kaufland Asia, the sourcing arm for Schwarz Group, a food and retail industry leader in Europe.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This has allowed our companies to scale and gain access to the European market, leveraging on Lidl & Kaufland's extensive consumer base.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Companies that are further along in their growth and internationalisation journeys often require bespoke support to fully unlock their potential and develop into truly global companies.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: One such example is Sing Fuels, a home-grown marine bunker and lubricant trader that supplies to more than 350 ports globally.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Through its partnership in Scale-Up, our flagship programme to support high-growth enterprises, Sing Fuels has sharpened its business growth plans, developed a market entry strategy into Africa for the lubricant business and also set up a clean energy arm, which trades and undertakes research and development into more sustainable fuels.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Sing Fuels is also leveraging on EDB's Corporate Venture Launchpad to develop a technology platform that addresses operational and capital challenges in the marine fuel industry.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We hope to support more local companies like Sing Fuels, which fly Singapore's flag high internationally while contributing significantly to our economy and creating good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We introduced the Singapore Global Enterprises (SGE) initiative at the COS last year to build a strong slate of locally-grown high-growth companies that can compete against the best in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The needs of these companies will differ vastly and they often require dedicated and customised support to meet their specific challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Building upon the flagship Scale-Up programme, Enterprise Singapore will partner these companies on their growth journeys in the following ways.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: First, we will continue to strengthen and deepen the companies' capabilities in developing new products, penetrating new markets and improving their work processes.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To help them build sustained innovation as a core competitive strategy, we will support them in undertaking R&D and innovation activities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will also support companies in expanding their global footprint and diversifying their supply chains.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To facilitate this, companies may receive customised financial support from Enterprise Singapore, such as through the co-funding of the establishment of their in-house R&D and innovation centres and efforts to build supply chain resilience.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Second, we will develop and deepen our talent pool.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Existing schemes like the Singapore Global Executive Programme help local high-growth companies enhance their human capital capabilities and attractiveness as employers.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will also expand the coverage of the Skills Future Enterprise Credit to include Scale-Up and the Singapore Global Executive Programme.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will allow eligible employers to use their credit to offset qualifying expenses under these programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For the more ambitious companies, we will give them an additional boost through the SGE initiative so that they may become global leaders in their respective fields.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I look forward to the rise of a new generation of SGEs as more Singapore companies make their mark globally.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will be with you every step of the way.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our efforts under the Singapore Economy 2030 vision can only be achieved if we have a high-quality workforce with industry-relevant skill sets and capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As the structural shifts that I had earlier described take root in our economy, we can expect existing jobs to be transformed at a faster pace even as new jobs are being created.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ms Mariam Jaafar and Prof Koh Lian Pin asked specifically how the Government is equipping the Singapore workforce to take on jobs in the green economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To prepare companies and workers for the transition to a greener future, the Government has worked with tripartite partners to roll out training programmes at various levels, including broader-based courses such as Enterprise Singapore's Enterprise Sustainability Programmes for business executives and sector-specific programmes such as Workforce Singapore's Career Conversion Programme for sustainability professionals.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Second Minister Tan See Leng and Minister of State Alvin Tan will share more on our efforts to ensure our workforce is well equipped to take on the opportunities under our Singapore Economy 2030 vision.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: However, we must not lose sight of the longer-term future.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Companies and workers alike must be prepared and ready for transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: If there is one thing the COVID-19 pandemic has taught us, it is that when the situation calls for it, Singapore as a country and Singaporeans can be agile and resilient, prepared to make difficult decisions for the greater good and help one another along the way.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: All of us – employers, workers, unions, trade associations and the Government – can all do our part to ensure that Singapore continues to punch above our weight on the global stage and build a strong and vibrant economy for our future generations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, last year, I announced the Enterprise 2030 strategy to build and sustain a vibrant ecosystem of Singapore enterprises that are future-ready and able to compete globally.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Minister Gan shared our plans to groom the most promising local enterprises into Singapore Global Enterprises.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I will elaborate on how we are helping these and other local enterprises to thrive.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will do so by supporting firms to maximise their human capital and develop innovation capabilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Singapore has consistently invested in our human capital through upskilling our workforce and remaining open to world-class talent.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It has allowed us to grow a vibrant business and trading hub, with competitive Singaporean enterprises and good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Look at the data over the last decade.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This translates into a cumulative growth of almost 30% over 10 years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is real income growth with the effect of inflation already accounted for.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Real resident household incomes have also risen across the same period.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Benchmarked against Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) countries, our resident employment rate is among the highest while our resident unemployment rate has remained among the lowest.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These have arisen because of the policies which we have put in place over the years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: By investing in ourselves and in our people, while remaining open to global talent and global businesses, we have grown the pie and created good outcomes for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Ms Jessica Tan and Mr Shawn Huang asked about the tight labour market and what businesses can do to adjust to manpower challenges.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These are targeted at various levels of talent within our enterprises, all the way from the intern to the CEO.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: First, the Enterprise Leadership for Transformation programme (ELT).

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: ELT is targeted at the senior leadership of our promising SMEs – the owners, the founders or successors and key members of their management.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: ELT supports these business leaders to achieve the next bound of growth by helping them develop their business strategies and leadership capabilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: ELT was first announced at Committee of Supply 2020 as a three-year pilot.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: One such example is 1-Group, a homegrown lifestyle, F&B and hospitality group with over 30 brands under its portfolio.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Through the ELT programme, the company sharpened its Southeast Asia internationalisation strategy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Leveraging new contacts made from an ELT market immersion trip to Vietnam, 1-Group has successfully partnered an in-market hospitality solutions company to expand into Vietnam.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This will allow more SME business leaders to benefit from the programme.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Launched in 2020, the Tech@SG pilot is targeted to support high-growth tech startups as part of their expansion in or foray into Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Under Tech@SG, they can secure up to 10 new Employment Passes (EP) for their core team members.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In the past three years since its launch, over 100 companies have come onboard.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These companies span across 13 different countries and across domains such as fintech, e-commerce and cybersecurity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Together, these Tech@SG companies have created more than 1,500 local jobs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is in spite of the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is a testament to Singapore's continued attractiveness to global talent.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: SpeQtral is a local startup founded in 2018 that has benefited from Tech@SG.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It is a spin-off from the Centre for Quantum Technologies at NUS, SpeQtral specialises in quantum key distribution.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is a nascent technology that enables users to establish secure communications networks with an additional quantum-secured encryption layer.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: SpeQtral came onboard as a Tech@SG firm in December 2021 and has since tapped on the programme to bring in external experts in this nascent field.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: At the same time, it has also hired locally to expand its footprint here in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: There will be no change to the qualifying criteria to ensure selectivity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Schemes like Tech@SG must be complemented by training of local talent, which we will continue to support through schemes like the TechSkills Accelerator (TeSA) programme operated by IMDA.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In time, locals will be able to take on these technology jobs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This scheme is targeted at fresh and recent local graduates.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This programme will support such young local talent to pursue structured career progression pathways in high-growth companies, including rotations to core functions and global attachments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I had announced this at the COS last year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I am glad to share that the programme was launched last December.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Launched in 2019, this programme aims to build a talent pipeline to support Singapore enterprises with their overseas expansion.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It does so by co-funding local, young talent to take on both local and overseas internships.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To date, the programme has supported over 19,000 internships in over 2,500 local companies despite the disruptions brought about by COVID-19.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Now that the countries across the world have reopened their borders, EnterpriseSG (ESG) is further curating the GRT to ensure it remains relevant and nimble in the post-COVID-19 new normal.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: So, in summary, the four schemes I have described – the ELT, the Tech@SG, the SGEP and GRT – all these schemes will allow our enterprises to maximise their human capital at all levels – from the intern to the CEO.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These enterprise-specific schemes complement the broader manpower schemes which we have in place, for example, the ONE Pass and COMPASS, and which I will give an update on in my Ministry of Manpower (MOM) COS speech tomorrow.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: My hope is that this suite of policies which MTI and MOM have worked closely together will help us to unlock the human capital that Singapore requires for our next phase of growth.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To realise our Singapore Economy 2030 vision, we need to continue to invest in our collective human capital.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We must be willing to learn, to imbibe, from the best by remaining open to global talent.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And we need to push the boundaries and we should not be afraid to take risks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And this brings me to my second point, which is on innovation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Ms Janet Ang and Mr Shawn Huang have asked about MTI’s efforts in developing innovation capabilities in our enterprises.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE) 2025, we are striving towards expanding the base of innovative enterprises and enabling the creation of globally competitive products and services out of Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: First, we are working with enterprises to strengthen their capability and capacity for market-oriented innovation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Second, we are scaling up and strengthening the Innovation and Enterprise (I&E) platforms to enable enterprises to better tap on our public research institutions and other innovation ecosystem players.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Third, we are forging strong connections to major innovation hubs and key demand markets.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In particular, innovation conducted through our polytechnics and the Institutes of Technical Education (ITEs) will now benefit from tax deductions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The same will also apply for innovation conducted through our existing Centres of Innovation (COIs) set up in partnership with selected polytechnics and A*STAR’s SIMTech.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Previously, some of these innovation activities may not have qualified for tax deductions for R&D.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This new provision will encourage our businesses, especially SMEs, to kickstart their innovation journey by tapping on the technical know-how and capabilities within these partner institutions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Hence, I look forward to more translational outcomes from such private-public collaborations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Beyond financial support, many companies are also looking for advice and strategic direction to guide their investments in innovation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This programme supports companies in partnering industry veterans to develop and to bring to market differentiated product offerings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The programme is run by IPI, which is a subsidiary of EnterpriseSG.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: ProfilePrint is a local agrifood tech enterprise that has benefited.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: ProfilePrint engaged the assistance of Innovation Advisor, Mr Phey Teck Moh, a seasoned mentor and angel investor, to help review their business model and go-to-market plans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Beyond these enterprise-centric programmes, we also have broader programmes to develop the innovation and enterprise ecosystem.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Last October, I was happy to launch the Technology for Enterprise Capability Upgrading, or T-Up Eagles Award.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This recognises students’ achievements and contributions to our SMEs during their work attachments under the T-Up Integrated Work Study Programme (IWSP).

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Now under this programme, seconded A*STAR researchers get to work closely with students from the Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT) attached to the same SME.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And since the programme’s launch about two years ago, 24 SIT students have benefitted from this mentorship.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I hope this will address Prof Hoon Hian Teck’s questions on how we are developing young talent.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For mid-career professionals, we have the Innovation and Enterprise Fellowship Programme (IFP).

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Launched in 2020, the IFP is a 12- to 18-month training programme administered by SGInnovate and is aimed at developing local talent or Fellows.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mid-career professionals, including Researchers, Scientists and Engineers (RSEs), who are selected as Fellows will be trained to become “ambidextrous”, familiar with both technology and business aspects in areas such as cybersecurity, robotics and biomedical sciences.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: IFP has achieved positive results in the past three years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Dr Yvonne Koh, who holds a PhD in Microbiology, is one of the Fellows who have benefited from this programme.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Under the IFP, Dr Koh joined Lightstone Singapore, which is a venture capital firm that invests in life sciences technologies and companies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The experience provided her with exposure to a global venture investment team.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: After Dr Koh graduated from the IFP in November 2021, Lightstone Singapore offered her a position as an investment professional, where she continues to source and assess global investment opportunities, and also support new company creation in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This means an increased capacity to take on and benefit more local talent.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These are significant moves that underscore our commitment to support firms in innovation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Last year, I explained the various emergency measures we took to manage the energy crisis.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These measures have stabilised the electricity markets for now, but this is unlikely to be the last energy crunch that we will see, as the world embarks on its energy transition.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Ms Mariam Jaafar and Ms Jessica Tan asked how Singapore would safeguard our energy security with increased volatility in global energy markets and advance our energy transition at the same time.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: MTI is adopting three key strategies to support the critical transformation needed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: First, developing new energy supply sources to diversify and decarbonise our energy supply.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Second, strengthening our energy market structure so as to ensure that the market continues to function well under volatile conditions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And third, building strong international collaborations to secure our energy supply and our energy technologies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Currently, Singapore relies on natural gas for about 95% of our power generation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will improve the energy efficiency of new and repowered natural gas power generation units through new emission standards.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: However, further abatement and diversification of our energy supply will need to be achieved through tapping on renewable energy both within Singapore and beyond our shores, and through the use of new low-carbon alternatives.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: First, Singapore is tapping on regional power grids to access cleaner energy sources abroad.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This will constitute around 30% of Singapore's electricity supply then.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To date, EMA has received more than 20 proposals under its Request for Proposal, or RFP, to import electricity to Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: EMA remains on track to meet our imports target.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Over the last two weeks, several companies have submitted their final proposals for large scale electricity imports from various countries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Projects which received support from the source countries and meet our requirements will receive EMA's conditional approval.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We expect to grant the first conditional approval soon.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To prepare for the large-scale imports, EMA is also conducting smaller-scale trials.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Such projects will help us learn, build confidence and pave the way for our larger scale electricity import projects.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These include the Lao PDR-Thailand-Malaysia-Singapore Power Integration Project, which commenced on 23 June 2022.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In addition, YTL Power Seraya and Tenaga Nasional Berhad Pasir Gudang Energy intend to export 100 megawatt of electricity from Malaysia to Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Last month, I witnessed their exchange of agreement ceremony with Malaysia's Minister of International Trade and Industry.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We hope to see this project commence this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Like LNG, hydrogen can be imported from various sources around the world, which enhances our energy security and our resilience.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It is also a potential alternative to fossil fuels in the maritime and aviation sectors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: A key prong of our strategy is to experiment with the use of advanced hydrogen technologies on the cusp of commercial readiness.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: EMA and MPA have launched an expression of interest for utilising ammonia for power generation and to support maritime bunkering needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Since then, we have received strong interest from industry players as well as international partners.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Third, we are accelerating solar deployment as we speak, and we are deploying energy storage systems to store and dispense intermittent solar power at different times to maintain grid reliability.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As of end 2022, we have deployed around 800 megawatt-peak (MWp) of solar power, compared to around 500 MWp in mid-2021.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As of the first half of last year, Singapore is already one of the most solar dense cities int he world and we are on track to achieving our solar panel deployment target of at least 2 gigawatt-peak (GWp) by 2030.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Earlier this month, I also officially launched a 285-megawatt hour (MWh) energy storage system on Jurong Island, which can meet the electricity needs of around 24,000 4-room HDB households for one day, in a single discharge.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Lastly, we are exploring if other forms of low-carbon energy supply, such as nuclear and geothermal are suitable for Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Abdul Samad asked what job opportunities will arise from new energy solutions and what we are doing to prepare our workforce for these jobs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: New energy solutions, such as solar, energy storage systems and smart grids, will create more skilled jobs for our workforce, including Power System Integration engineers and Energy Storage System software developers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As Ms Poh Li San has rightfully pointed out, Singapore should invest more in talent development for our energy transition.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The new Green Skills Committee that Minister Gan mentioned will identify and develop more programmes for newer forms of energy technology, like hydrogen and carbon capture as they become ready.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Speaking in both my capacities as Second Minister for Trade and Industry and the Minister for Manpower, we are aligned.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And I urge all of our workers to join these programmes to reskill and upskill in clean energy areas.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I would also like to join and echo Mr Abdul Samad in extending our acknowledgement and appreciation to our workers in the power and gas industries, who worked hard to ensure that we had uninterrupted gas and electricity supply during the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Abdul Samad suggested a one-time reward for power and gas workers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: During the pandemic, many of our essential workers stepped forward to play their part.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our healthcare workers, in particular, served at the frontline against COVID-19.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The COVID-19 Healthcare Award announced in November 2021 was in recognition of our healthcare workers' contributions and dedication.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I would encourage employers in the power and gas industries to consider the contributions of their workers and to fairly recognise and reward their workers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The global energy market continue be turbulent in the coming years because of geopolitics and climate action.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But based on what we have learnt from the recent energy crisis, we will update our regulatory approach to strengthen the foundations of our energy market.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I hope that this will address Ms Poh Li San and Dr Lim Wee Kiak's query if Singapore has a fallback plan should there be disruptions to our energy supplies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are also exploring ways to centrally aggregate gas procurement and obtain more secure and longer-term contracts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: EMA is seeking feedback on the proposed enhancements and plans to announce the final changes later in the year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The energy transition is challenging, given the increased volatility in global energy markets.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: No one country can do it alone, and we need to work together to advance our collective interests.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Singapore has partnered with like-minded countries to support one another in our decarbonisation efforts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Last year, we signed Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) on energy cooperation with Indonesia, Brunei, Cambodia, Lao PDR and Vietnam.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have also signed Memoranda of Cooperation with Japan and a Green Economy Agreement with Australia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These G2G partnerships have helped to facilitate commercial collaborations, which demonstrate the interest and viability of renewable energy co-development projects for cross-border electricity trade.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Not only will they help to unlock the region's renewable energy potential, which can serve the domestic demand of source countries, they can also catalyse economic growth, by stimulating clean energy investment flows and generating new green jobs in source countries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To boost the viability of clean energy trade projects, Singapore is also partnering with the US on a Feasibility Study on Regional Energy Connectivity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is part of the US' Net Zero World Initiative.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The US will collaborate with Singapore and Southeast Asian partners to explain the benefits of greater connectivity, as well as assess the technical, legal, and commercial steps that we need to take to realise ASEAN's vision of a regional power grid network.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We should not forget the role that international organisations also play.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: They shape our understanding of the dynamism in global energy markets and they help us to seize opportunities in the energy transition.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Last year, we announced that Singapore and the IEA, or the International Energy Agency, are exploring the possibility of establishing a regional cooperation centre here in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This will help broaden IEA's outreach to the Asia-Pacific and accelerate the region's low-carbon energy transitions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Singapore also has strong partnerships with the International Renewable Energy Agency, or IRENA.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will continue strengthen and broaden our relationship with them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The global energy transition is a challenging but critical undertaking that the world will need to manage this existential climate crisis.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: MTI will work closely with our industry stakeholders and our international partners to enhance our energy resilience in a low-carbon world.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Ms Janet Ang asked how we can help businesses through this transition.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I have shared at length at how we are transforming the way in which we produce electricity and energy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: (In Mandarin):   As the Chinese saying goes, "When you are constrained, be flexible and be willing to make changes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: If you change, you can find a solution, and its effects can last a long time." Singapore lacks natural resources.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Together, with all of your support, we will continue to build a better, a more resilient and an even more vibrant Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, Minister Tan reminded us to keep an eye on the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Earlier, both Ministers offered a glimpse by outlining our trade and enterprise strategies under our Singapore Economy 2030 vision.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I will share about the other two pillars under this vision, which Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Ms Jessica Tan asked about.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Manufacturing remains the bedrock of our economy, forming its largest component.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our established strength in manufacturing has allowed our economy to remain resilient in spite of the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In 2021, we launched our Manufacturing 2030 vision to grow our value-added (VA) by 50% from 2020 to 2030.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In 2022, our manufacturing VA increased by more than 15% from 2020.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To have enough workers to fill these newly created jobs, we will partner industry to develop a strong talent pipeline.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are working with trade associations and chambers like the Singapore Precision Engineering and Technology Association (SPETA) and the Singapore Semiconductor Industry Association to offer quality internship opportunities for Institute of Technical Education (ITE) students to raise job awareness of and enhance these students' experience in the sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As of September last year, we have created 806 internship opportunities across 71 companies, exceeding our target of securing 200 internships across 50 companies by end 2022.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Last year, Deputy Prime Minister Heng and I, together with SPETA and the Institute for Human Resource Professionals, launched our Manufacturing Employers' Handbook, which provides companies with human capital best practices and tools to help them structure career progression pathways for their employees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Despite a more challenging global environment, we plan to continue growing our manufacturing sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: First, we will do even more to attract frontier investments here.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We remain an attractive manufacturing location for many best-in-class firms like BioNTech, which chose to locate here because of our strong fundamentals, like our pro-business environment and a strong rule of law.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will continue to strengthen our manufacturing ecosystem and toolkits to maintain our competitiveness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This further reinforces our commitment to strengthen incentives to attract leading edge investments here.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Prof Hoon Hian Teck also asked how we are creating the manpower required for Manufacturing 2030.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The short answer is we will attract more Singaporeans to the sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: First, we piloted the Accelerated Pathways for Technicians and Assistant Engineers (Manufacturing) Grant to help selected manufacturing companies hire, train and offer career progression for ITE graduates to become proficient technicians in the sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will extend this pilot by another two years to March 2025 to allow even more companies to be onboarded.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa, Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Ms Jessica Tan asked about emerging sectors in Singapore and opportunities for businesses in those areas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Shawn Huang is right also to highlight the potential of robotics and space.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We aim to be a frontrunner for tech-enabled manufacturing in areas like biotech and robotics while also exploring the space industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: On biotech, our biotech sector may be nascent but we expect it to grow by 8% annually.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Ms He Ting Ru asked about the opportunities and support to further develop this sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: A*STAR's Singapore Therapeutics Development Review (STDR) initiative and Technology for Enterprise Capability Upgrading (T-Up) programme is one such thing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Since 2003, more than 950 A*STAR research scientists and engineers have been seconded to support over 850 local SMEs in product development under T-Up.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Of this pool, close to 70 of them have been seconded to 45 biotech-related companies and 16 have joined the companies full-time at the end of their T-Up projects.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: One example is A*STAR scientist Dr Lionel Low, who was seconded in 2019 to Tessa Therapeutics.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Dr Low has now since joined Tessa Therapeutics full-time as Director of Research and Development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Minister Tan also announced that we are expanding our Innovation and Enterprise Fellowship Programme (IFP) to include public sector partners like the Experimental Drug Development Centre.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The second thing that we are doing is to grow our biotech venture ecosystem financing and funding.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are working with venture capitalists (VCs) to channel more investments into Singapore-based biotech startups.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In 2021 and 2022, Enterprise Singapore's SEEDS Capital invested $70 million and catalysed another $300 million from 40 private equity and VC funds into 70 deep-tech startups while Startup SG Tech extended $10 million in funding to 30 projects.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Just as our biotech sector is showing promise, we are also making strides in robotics.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Singapore has the second most robot-intensive manufacturing sector in the world, just after South Korea.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our manufacturing, construction and healthcare sectors here use robots to improve productivity, safety and quality.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In manufacturing and construction, robots can ease on-site manpower constraints.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For example, construction company Gammon uses Spot, a four-legged robot built by Boston Dynamics to scan sections of mud and gravel at construction sites to check work progress.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will strengthen our national robotics ecosystem through the National Robotics Programme (NRP).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In fact, last month, Minister Tan and I celebrated NRP's sixth anniversary at Singapore University of Technology & Design (SUTD) with startups and industry players.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: There is great energy and promise in our robotics sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our biotech and robotics solutions have applications for the silver industry too – a sector Ms Sylvia Lim asked about.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For example, Alexandra Hospital successfully trialed Florence, a robotic nursing assistant co-created with NCS to perform tasks, including taking vital signs of patients at their bedside and delivering medication and items.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This frees up time for nurses to perform other value-added tasks for their patients.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Another example is MiRXES, a homegrown A*STAR spin off firm that focuses on early detection of cancer using its proprietary microRNA platform.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Enterprise Singapore's Scale-up SG programme helped MiRXES internationalise and expand to North and Southeast Asia in 2022.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: These firms are doing good work to help address challenges in ageing societies like ours and in many parts of the world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will continue to help them thrive in this emerging global silver industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We have seen how tech-enabled manufacturing solutions improve the lives in the silver industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This also inspires us to explore new frontiers like space.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We thank Mr Shawn Huang for acknowledging the space industry's growth potential.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We have been gradually growing our space industry since the early 2000s.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In 2013, we established our national space office – the Office for Space Technology and Industry (OSTIn).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: OSTIn brings together players from different disciplines to build our nascent space ecosystem and develop emerging and disruptive technologies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We have good local capabilities in satellite engineering, remote sensing and satellite communications (satcom) and have launched over 15 satellites thus far.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: DSO National Laboratories collaborated with OSTIn, local space research partners and international industry partners to launch our first locally developed Synthetic Aperture Radar microsatellite into space last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We can also apply space-based technologies to other sectors such as aviation and maritime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our space industry has also created attractive jobs and anchored foreign companies here.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Today, we have approximately 2,000 professionals and researchers in our space sector and more than 60 local and international space companies based here.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As I see our students strolling in, please come and join our space sector and join our rocket ship.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We have made good progress for Manufacturing 2030, including in biotech, robotics and space.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As we programme our satnav back to Earth, let us land on Services 2030 – our plan to grow our services sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Derrick Goh asked how we have been helping our SMEs digitalise.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our Services 2030 vision is to grow our services sectors by making them more digital and sustainable and to anchor Singapore as a leading hub for business, lifestyle and tourism.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: By 2030, we aim to entrench Singapore as a hub of firms, a hub of flows and a hub of talents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: A hub of firms – where we continue to attract multinational enterprises and large local enterprises to use Singapore as a base for their Global-Asia operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: A hub of flows – where we strengthen our position as a global trading, financial and lifestyle hub, build on our networks of international trade agreements to connect Singapore and Southeast Asia to the world and further our digital and green economy agreements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Minister Gan spoke of how our refreshed Professional Services Industry Transformation Map (ITM) will help our professional services firms transform so Singapore remains a hub for firms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To achieve this, our Professional Services ITM 2025 will focus on three areas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: First, we will strengthen Singapore's appeal as a business hub for companies to build their headquarters here.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Headquarters create meaningful jobs for Singaporeans in various areas, including corporate functions such as marketing, legal and finance and accounting.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We have a pool of ready talent to provide these services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are already attracting leading global firms because of the strong fundamentals I mentioned earlier, but to help existing headquarters in Singapore improve their in-house corporate functions, EDB has designed two online assessment tools for marketing and also for finance and accounting.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: These resources help companies assess their corporate functions and recommend ways to transform job roles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: EDB's Corporate Venture Launchpad also help Singapore-based companies nurture new venture concepts here.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: SembCorp Industries Ltd has benefited from this programme and spun off new ventures.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Second, we will help our professional services SMEs become more digital.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: If you are a professional services SME, please continue to use our Productivity Solutions Grant and Enterprise Development Grant and platforms like IMDA's Chief Technology Officer-as-a-Service.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Third, we will help our companies create jobs and upskill our workforce to meet rising demands in sustainability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: EDB is partnering consulting and engineering services firms to set up regional sustainability Centres of Excellence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: These centres will groom talent, develop sustainability expertise and drive R&D capabilities and activities for Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our Design Singapore Council has also developed the Good Design Research Initiative as well, to help designers and firms like Ginlee Studio and bioSEA design for environmental impact.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
