text: We will also help Singaporeans take on new jobs in the professional services sector by reskilling and redeploying workers through initiatives like our Career Conversion Programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For example, if you are looking to upskill and explore new roles in the accountancy sector, you can approach the Accountancy Careers Hub to pick up new skills and receive career guidance to advance your career within the industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: With these ITM 2025 building blocks in place, our professional services sector is looking professional and bright!

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Just as our Professional Services sector is distinguishing itself globally, a vibrant tourism scene will also differentiate us from other business hubs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In the next decade, we will build our tourism sector in three ways.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: First, we will continue to refresh and invest in new products and events.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This reflects strong confidence in our competitiveness as a top tourism destination and ensures we continue to have new and updated hotels, attractions and events.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will also partner world-class event organisers and frontload our investments to build a strong leisure and business events pipeline that appeal to different interests and sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This year, we welcome international leisure events debuting here, such as Van Gogh: The Immersive Experience and Sneaker Con Southeast Asia; and will witness the return of top business events like Gastech Exhibition & Conference.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As SportSG announced last November, Singapore will also host the inaugural Olympic Esports Week in June.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This has the potential to grow Singapore as an eSports Hub, attracting investments, creatives and talents in an emerging sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Second, we will continue to build our tourism businesses' tech capabilities and workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will partner industry to create virtual experiences and experiment with extended and augmented reality to complement real-world offerings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Singapore Tourism Board (STB) and Gardens by the Bay are currently trialing the Lost Fairy, an augmented reality storytelling experience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Visitors at the Floral Fantasy are transported into a magical fantasy world, providing a refreshing and gamified visitor experience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will also continue to help our tourism sector use tech to raise their productivity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This system uses facial recognition technology to authenticate guests' identities, verify the validity of their stay and automatically transmit relevant data to the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Guests will experience a more seamless check-in process with waiting time shortened by up to 70%.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will also continue to prepare our tourism workers for post-pandemic recovery.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our Enhanced Training Support Package provided close to 60,000 training places by end-2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: When borders reopened last year, STB and NTUC's e2i launched our Tourism Careers Hub to provide career coaching and employment and training support for our tourism workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As of end-2022, more than 500 workers were placed into our tourism sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Third, we have ambitions to be a globally known sustainable urban destination.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Last Friday, Senior Minister Teo spoke about our industry sectoral roadmaps that guide companies in their sustainability journey, including for tourism.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har also asked about developing sustainability roadmaps.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Last year, we launched our Hotel and Meetings, Incentives, Conferences & Exhibitions (MICE) Sustainability Roadmaps to help both these sectors build new green skills and track their carbon footprint.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Tech has also played a part in greening our tourism sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This certification validates our policies in stewarding Singapore to become a sustainable urban destination by 2030, in line with our Singapore Green Plan 2030.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Big Tiny operates sustainably through using renewable energy, energy efficient appliances and a biodigester which converts food from waste to compost on-site within 24 hours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In the coming months, we will also launch other offerings at Lazarus Island like non-motorised water activities and also glamping.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I hope our continued investment in our tourism businesses and workforce will give Members confidence that our tourism businesses are well-equipped to thrive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our efforts, to green our tourism sector is part of our larger plan to tackle climate change.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We remain committed to achieve net zero emissions by 2050 and have taken decisive steps towards our climate goals, which brings me to our Green Economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Prof Koh Lian Pin asked about the transition framework for companies in emissions-intensive trade-exposed sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The framework aims to help our businesses transition into low-carbon operations, while mitigating the risk of carbon leakage, which could happen when companies shift operations to other jurisdictions with lower or no effective carbon prices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It will be determined based on internationally recognised efficiency benchmarks, where available; or the facilities' decarbonisation plans that are aligned with our net zero commitments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are engaging affected companies on details of the transition framework, including how to apply these efficiency benchmarks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will finalise these details ahead of changes to the carbon tax regime taking place in 2024.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har, Ms Jessica Tan, Ms Janet Ang and Prof Koh asked how we are helping businesses transition to a low-carbon future and equipping our workforce for jobs in the green economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Members also asked how we are helping our SMEs embark on decarbonisation, carbon accounting and sustainability reporting.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We aim to transform our economy, work with the international community to achieve our collective climate targets and remain relevant in a low-carbon future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our Green Economy Strategy will help our businesses do so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: First, as we digitalise our economy, we are also greening our businesses and industries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will extend the enhanced support under our Enterprise Development Grant (EDG) for sustainability projects, to encourage more local companies to identify and seize opportunities in the green economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Sustainability reporting is increasingly important for companies to demonstrate their sustainability performance and commitment to the environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Consumers and investors want greater transparency through sustainability disclosures.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They are more conscious of the environmental and social impact of their products and investments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Companies can start by measuring carbon emissions, which will enable them to monitor, improve and subsequently report their sustainability impact.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: If you are an SME keen to measure your carbon emissions, please explore EnterpriseSG's Productivity Solutions Grant.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: EnterpriseSG and Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) will also continue to explore ways to support more advanced solutions through the Advanced Digital Solutions scheme, which we will announce details for in the second half of 2023.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: EnterpriseSG will also work with Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA) and industry partners to develop programmes to help enterprises embark on sustainability reporting.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will also help businesses strengthen their knowledge on sustainability through courses and new playbooks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: EnterpriseSG will develop new Enterprise Sustainability Programme (ESP) thematic courses in topics like Decarbonisation and Sustainable Finance, and expand the number of ESP Foundational Course partners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will announce new course providers and the new courses will commence in the second quarter of this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To complement this, EnterpriseSG will also develop playbooks for businesses to learn more about sustainability topics and how to take steps to become more sustainable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har also suggested building knowledge-sharing platforms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: She would be pleased to know that EnterpriseSG will set up a sustainability website for enterprises to access such resources.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Ms Foo also suggested helping companies test-bed new ideas and experiment with new technologies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In November, we launched Green Economy Regulatory Initiative (GERI) to speed up innovation in the green economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Derrick Goh asked how we are positioning Singapore as a leading international green hub.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We partner other countries to develop trusted and robust international markets for carbon credits.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, in conclusion, our journey may be fraught with challenges but it is also filled with opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As we write the next chapter of our economic story, we must build on our existing foundations, yet be bold enough to trailblaze new industries in this new era.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This will enable our businesses to capture new markets and position Singapore as the gateway to Southeast Asia, creating good jobs and opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Next, Minister of State Low Yen Ling will share how we will support our enterprises to weather the economic challenges and move forward together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, Minister Gan Kim Yong and Second Minister Tan See Leng have both shared about the Enterprise 2030 strategy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The vision and the plan is to build a vibrant ecosystem of Singapore enterprises that are future-ready and globally competitive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Shawn Huang asked about how Government has supported businesses throughout the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Throughout the crisis, the Government came up with many schemes to help businesses survive and adapt to the changing economic conditions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: First, we extended critical life support for major cost items that businesses needed to incur to stay up and running.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We launched the Jobs Support Scheme (JSS) in Budget 2020 to boost wage support for employers to help them keep their local employees in those uncertain times.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Second, we provided financing support to help ease the cashflow and financing constraints of businesses as they faced slowing economic growth, weaker trade and higher prices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Third, we enhanced our assistance for business transformation which was important for the survival and growth of our enterprises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Between 2020 and 2022, a total of 55,500 local companies embarked on productivity, capability development and internationalisation projects.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This year, we expect global growth to moderate amid tight financial market conditions and elevated energy prices as mentioned by Minister Gan and 2nd Minister.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As a result, business costs and cashflow constraints remain top of mind for our SMEs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We understand that being able to access financing is critical for our SMEs, critical for our businesses, as Mr Shawn Huang, Mr Derrick Goh and Ms He Ting Ru have highlighted in their cuts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to assure Members that MTI and our economic agencies – we will not let up our efforts to ensure that enterprises have suitable access to financing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Enterprise Financing Scheme (EFS) launched in 2019 to support companies in their various stages of growth has aided thousands of businesses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Ninety-nine percent of these companies were SMEs and the majority, or more than 80% of the applicants were successful in getting the funds they need.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The schemes are namely the EFS-SME Working Capital Loan, EFS-Trade Loan and EFS-Project Loan.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will extend the current enhanced maximum loan quantum parameters of $500,000 for the EFS-SME Working Capital Loan and $10 million for the EFS-Trade Loan.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For the EFS-Trade Loan, we will also maintain the current enhanced Government risk-share level at 70%.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The extension of these enhancements will help our enterprises cope with higher working capital and cashflow needs, given the current economic uncertainties and supply chain pressures that has led to lengthened payment cycles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Furthermore, we will extend the period of support for domestic construction projects under the EFS-Project Loan scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As the construction sector is still recovering from the pandemic, we will continue to support them to cope with the higher costs of construction materials.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This will enable our construction companies to secure vital financing to carry out existing projects and secure new ones, as construction activity steadily picks up the pace towards pre-pandemic levels.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: All of the enhancements that I have mentioned, the enhancement to our financing schemes will help our SMEs and businesses to cope with near-term cashflow constraints and secure necessary financing for different business needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The EFS-Venture Debt scheme was introduced in 2015 to help catalyse the Singapore market for venture debt, which is a form of alternative debt financing typically for high-growth startups.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To expand our support to a wider range of financing tools, the Government will enhance the EFS-Venture Debt programme to include venture debt loans that is backed by RCPS, which is Redeemable Convertible Preference Shares.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This will benefit startups that require more flexible loan repayment plans, including early-stage and high-growth startups in fast-expanding sectors, such as deep tech.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, the COVID-19 pandemic and the start of the Ukraine-Russia war last year have led to a heightened business cost environment in many parts of the world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Domestic energy and electricity prices are likely to remain elevated in the near term, as the global energy market stays volatile.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: On the back of steeper electricity and fuel costs, we launched EEG, Energy Efficiency Grant, five months ago in September 2022.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This grant provides local enterprises in the Food Services, Food Manufacturing and the Retail sectors with up to 70% support to invest in energy-efficient equipment in pre-scoped categories, such as LED lighting, air conditioners and refrigerators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The EEG complements our wide range of energy efficiency initiatives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For instance, the National Environment Agency (NEA)'s Energy Efficiency Fund supports businesses in the manufacturing sector, while the Building and Construction Authority (BCA)'s Green Mark Incentive Scheme for Existing Buildings 2.0 covers building owners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, we have the Resource Efficiency Grant for Emissions which targets emissions-intensive facilities, such as manufacturing facilities and data centres.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: On top of all these grants, we have the Energy Efficiency Technology Centre, which is a collaboration between NEA and SIT, the Singapore Institute of Technology, that help our SMEs make informed decisions on the measures they can take to improve their energy efficiency.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This will also enable companies in their transition to a lower-carbon future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment (MSE) will provide more details about the Government's plans for NEA's EEF.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to assure all Members that we are taking a holistic, whole-of-Government approach to encourage our businesses to adopt energy-efficient practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I am glad to report that many SMEs in the Food Manufacturing, Food Services and Retail sector, are tapping on EEG.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is a F&B business, which used EEG to buy an energy-efficient cooking hob for their restaurant that could cut their energy cost of cooking by some 30%.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Another company is food manufacturer Soltem Foods Pte Ltd, which bought energy-efficient refrigerators to reduce their power bills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to assure Members that MTI and all our economic agencies review the effectiveness of our various measures regularly and monitors the economic conditions closely.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will not hesitate to finetune our schemes or introduce new measures when the need arises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I have shared the Government's plans to bolster support for enterprises in the year ahead.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Since 2020, the GoBusiness portal has provided our SMEs with one-stop access to more than 100 Government support schemes and information on more than 200 licences that is issued by some 30 Government agencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, anyone starting a business can easily incorporate their company's business using the GoBusiness portal, as well as directly apply for the licences they need, all at their fingertips.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The portal's e-Adviser feature helps the businesses to identify the relevant support schemes for their needs, from eligibility criteria for grants and loans, to tax incentives and even business solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Last year, 40,000 businesses benefitted from the help that GoBusiness portal offers to select and apply for the right support scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, all this done at our fingertips, which translate to cost savings and time savings, which are very critical for SMEs owners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, Minister Gan spoke about the importance of taking a hard look at how companies can transform their businesses to take advantage of new growth opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We strongly encourage all Singapore enterprises who are looking for support to grow their business, to scale their business, to get onto the GoBusiness.gov.sg to tap onto the available help.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In my Committee of Supply (COS) speech last year, I talked about how the heartland enterprises constitute an important fabric of our society, because they inject vibrancy into our neighbourhoods, they provide jobs and opportunities for promising local businesses to grow.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In a midst of a changing consumer and enterprise landscape, heartland enterprises need to stay relevant and competitive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Over the past 12 months, Our Heartlands 2025 have made great strides across three focus areas: one, deepening the digital and manpower capabilities of heartland shops; two, upgrading the capabilities of the trade associations and chambers (TACs) to better support the enterprises; and three, revitalising the heartlands to improve liveliness and attract more customers into our heartland shops, our precinct.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As Mr Derrick Goh pointed out, there still lies a great potential for heartland enterprises to innovate, digitalise and to build capabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The transformation of our heartlands is a multi-year effort, and we will continue to help our heartland enterprises sharpen their competitive edge and improve their skill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Heartland enterprises have made significant progress to upgrade their digital capabilities since the launch of Heartlands Go Digital in October 2020.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, two-thirds are onboard various digital platforms, such as Google Business Profile, Carousell, Fave, Shopback and so on, to serve their customers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This shop participated in the Heartlands Go Digital programme in 2022 last year to onboard their business onto the Fave digital platform.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Within just six months, World Teahouse observe an average 25% increase in a customers' spending per e-Fave transaction.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The use of Fave eCards allowed the tea house to reach out to the platform's large and younger consumer base.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: While many heartland enterprises are content with their current suite of digital solutions, some are ready to do even more.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Heartlands Go Digital 3.0 will expand partnerships with new private sector partners and Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) to deepen the digital and manpower capabilities of our heartland shops across a holistic range of capability development areas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And this includes digital marketing, visual merchandising, service excellence and financial management know-how provided through business advisory services, in-shop training and group-based upgrading projects across different precincts and trades.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We want to encourage more innovative shops to embark on product or business model innovations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In recent years, specific initiatives, such as the Heartland Innovation Challenge and Visual Merchandising Programme, have supported many heartland enterprises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Earlier on, hon Member Ms Janet Ang highlighted SOVEG, which is a type of meatless satay and Hot SpicyMama condiments, all during lunchtime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I thought I would top it off with a gelato example.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is a local company, a gelato shop that is called Denzy Collective and they are a heartland shop.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They collaborated with Tampines West Merchants' Association (TWMA) and Temasek Polytechnic to create fresh gelato flavours sustainably.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Using blemished fruits supplied by the merchants in Tampines West, Denzy Collective transformed these ingredients into a new, exotic flavour of gelato called Christmas Orange.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And with the help of Temasek Polytechnic, the new gelato was launched with very attractive branding and marketing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I know it is 2.00 pm, hang in there.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And to let our Members savour this very refreshing innovation, we have arranged for Denzy Collective's Christmas Orange gelato to be served in the Parliament's Members Room immediately after MTI's COS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We hope all the Members will enjoy it and continue to extend your support to all our heartland enterprises as they strive to improve, innovate and delight their customers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, I have set aside two cups for you, to thank you for your chairmanship.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Building on the momentum of all these efforts, we hope to spur greater innovations and entrepreneurships in our heartlands.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Through this programme, we aim to address two specific challenges that heartland enterprises continue to face: one, access to shop and retail spaces in heartland precincts to test innovative ideas; and two, access to resources for innovation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: First, we will construct and make available modular temporary spaces in mature heartland precincts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This will complement HDB's efforts to provide access to flexible shop and retail spaces across precincts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Senior Minister of State Sim Ann will announce the details of the scheme as part of the Ministry of National Development's COS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Second, we will provide a conducive ecosystem to build enterprise innovation capabilities and scale.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This includes a range of innovation and entrepreneurship courses conducted by partners, such as IHLs and the Heartland Enterprise Centre, Singapore (HECS) to build our enterprises' know-how and knowledge.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Furthermore, we will offer opportunities for heartland shopkeepers and merchants to learn from the best practices of successful entrepreneurs who are familiar or well-versed in the heartlands, and know the merchants' association and the community well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, as we broaden our support for heartland enterprises, we are also deepening partnerships with key partners to boost our drive for transformation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: All over the world, the pace of digital acceleration is happening.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our enterprises must continue to adapt and transform to stay relevant and competitive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government recognises that it cannot drive business transformation efforts alone.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We need like-minded partners to work with us to multiply our outreach and support more enterprises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Central to this approach are our trade associations and chambers (TACs).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: TACs will continue to be the torchbearers for new industry initiatives and we remain committed to strengthening these partnerships with them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Several Members of Parliament, including Mr Raj Joshua Thomas and Mr Desmond Choo, asked about how we can boost the capabilities of TACs and how these organisations can take on more roles in the industry and enterprise transformation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We have been doing this and will continue to do more.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In 2022, the Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCCI) launched the TAC Competency Framework and Growth Model that Mr Thomas talked about.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This provides resources for TACs to identify existing gaps and the critical skills they need for their growth journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: At the COS last year, I also announced three initiatives to strengthen our TACs' human capital and digital capabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, the next generation of TAC leaders comprising 10 TAC Fellows from eight different TACs are being groomed and developed under the TAC Fellowship Programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As part of the six-month programme, they will co-create solutions together to address common challenges and develop ideas to capture new opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our network of 11 SME Centres partner our TACs to uplift and support our SMEs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Through SGTech, we will intensify our bottom-up industry efforts to spur enterprise digitalisation with a "3S" framework: (a) strategy; (b) solution; and (c) skills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This new centre represents SGTech's strong commitment to spurring enterprise digitalisation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It also builds on SGTech's past efforts like its partnership with Meta and Enterprise Singapore to help local SMEs leverage technology to transform and prepare for the post-COVID-19 economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The other key opportunity area that we will focus on is sustainability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Moving ahead, the Alliance will kickstart initiatives to uplift the sustainability capabilities of other TACs and their members.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, SGTech will develop a guided programme for SMEs to reduce their environmental footprint.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Sustainable Energy Association of Singapore will advise on energy solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We encourage other TACs to join in and tap on this Sustainability Alliance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, there are many pockets of opportunities for enterprises to develop their competence, expand overseas and transform.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The various initiatives helmed by our TACs are vital stepping stones to attain greater heights.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We would like to spur our enterprises to take advantage of these opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: On this note, the Government is also committed to deepening our partnership with the industry and TACs to enhance consumer protection.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Fair trading practices and strong consumer confidence are key pillars of a healthy economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MTI regularly reviews our consumer protection regime to ensure that consumers' interests are safeguarded.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As we continue to examine the current policies, we are prepared to do more to strengthen our consumer protection regime without affecting well-intentioned businesses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will continue to work closely with our partners, including CASE, in this effort.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, as we close ranks in partnership with our enterprises and our TACs, we have made steady progress on our journey to transform and to seek new growth potential.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Together, we can face the challenges ahead and ride new waves of opportunity and new waves of change as one people, in partnership and in solidarity, to overcome and succeed as one.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Minister Gan spoke about MTI's effort to strengthen trade connectivity and support for our companies going international.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Given our external developments and as part of the Resilience Measures, I think it is important to also anchor ourselves as a hub for global traders.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: How has that helped us grow our trade volumes and also expanded our external trade with the rest of the world?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Mr Chairman, let me thank Mr Liang for his question.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Indeed, I talked about Trade 2030 last year.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This year, I had intended to give an update, but the Chairman is very strict on guillotine times.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, I do not have the space to squeeze in —

speaker: The Chairman
text: Two cups of ice cream and you will get two minutes.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, in exchange for two cups of ice cream, he has given me two more minutes.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I will use these two minutes to explain our Trade 2030 strategy.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I introduced it last year and we have made good progress.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Particularly, we also have brought in several global traders, like Mr Liang pointed out, that will help us anchor ourselves in the global supply chain.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They have decided to set up Asia Pacific headquarters in Singapore to conduct their trade in the region.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Despite COVID-19, they have decided to expand their trade network and use Singapore as an anchor.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: There are also new opportunities emerging from sustainability.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have a Spanish company called Cepsa, which has also expanded their operation in Singapore and is looking at using Singapore as their Asia trading hub.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: These all work towards strengthening Singapore's position as a trading centre.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We are also encouraging our traders to not just do trade as traditional trading activities but to look at innovation, develop new products of their own so that they become the leaders in this particular field that they are specialised in.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This company has been working on innovation with our research institutions and tried to develop new products.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They are also working with our restaurants to see how they can develop food that is more sustainable, that caters not only to the Asian palate but are also more convenient and healthier editions of the food, in line with the Healthier SG approach.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think these are innovations that we will encouraged our traders to embark on so that they develop their own products and services and become leaders in their own field.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think through this, we will continue to grow our trading hub status.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: The first is in regard to the Green Skills Committee that the Minister mentioned earlier.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: How is it different from the Jobs-Skills Integrator?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: I think what would be interesting would be to note what age groups will be impacted, whether they will benefit from this as well?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Because I think Minister of State Alvin Tan mentioned that there are 850 internships for ITE students.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: So, the question is whether there will be ITE absorption into the manufacturing sector and also into the green sector.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: My second question is in regard to Minister Tan's answer.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: I think he elaborated about the green transition, the carbon transition, the energy transition.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: My question is going forward, beyond this Budget, will there be any additional spending on physical infrastructure needed for the energy transition as Singapore prepares to absorb some of this solar and other alternative energy inputs coming to Singapore going forward?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: What is our strategy on that front and our spending needs?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Jobs-Skills Integrators will serve sectors which are a little bit more fragmented and less regulated, such as precision engineering, retail, wholesale, trade.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The GSC is different in such that the focus will be on emerging green skills.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: These are in areas of green growth opportunities such as smart grid technology, even for workers that are graduating from Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) or ITEs, for example, in electric vehicle (EV) technology.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The committee will need to map this green skills development with a framework and a training roadmap and size the implementation and training needs as the economy grows in this regard.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The GSC will focus first on two green skill areas, as the Minister mentioned.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: First is on sustainability reporting and assurance and the second is on energy.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We are looking at skills on the first front – sustainability reporting, disclosures, advisory and compliance.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So that is one sector, one first key area.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We know that and we envision that there will be a demand for skills associated with generation storage and deployment of renewable energy, for example, battery energy storage systems design, modelling and simulation and distributed energy resources management.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, sustainability reporting and assurance first because this is emerging and, of course, as infrastructure changes, energy as well.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To support our energy transition, there are a couple of initiatives that we are doing.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: One, obviously, is, as I have said in my speech, in terms of coming up with our energy market structure where we require the generation companies (gencos), in terms of the upgrading of CCGTs, to move to a more energy-efficient and lower emission, type of newer generation CCGTs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As a result of that we will request for proposals and interests.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The change in terms of the markets, in terms of our regulation, allows us to plant that capacity, in the event that our existing gencos do not want to participate in it.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: If you talked about the kind of costing, at this particular point in time, given the fact that as a result of providing more market certainty to all of our gencos, we think that there is a higher chance of them participating in the RFP to build these new CCGTs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: On the second part of it, in terms of our resilience, given the heightened uncertainties, the volatilities in the energy market, we need to also ramp up our capacity for standby facility.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For instance, we have a standby LNG storage facility to ensure that we will not in any way be compromised if there are shortages in terms of the global supply chain.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The third part is that we will also continue to invest in our grid development as well as energy storage systems and in terms of building interconnectors, when we import renewable energy from around the region.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will be providing more insights throughout the year in successive meetings.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I hope that gives you a bit of a preamble as to what is to come.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: I am very glad to hear that TACs have been helping our companies to digitise and be more sustainable.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: Can I check with Minister of State Low Yen Ling how the Ministry is helping TACs to play an advisory role to support our businesses to internationalise?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Mr Chairman, I want to thank the Member, Mr Desmond Choo for his clarification.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I had intended to respond to those questions that he mentioned in the cuts, but I sort of ran out speech time.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, allow me to very quickly and succinctly reply to him.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure Mr Desmond Choo and the Members that we are working hand-in-hand with our various TACs to support the growth and expansion of our Singapore enterprises overseas.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And if you think about it, fortunately we started that before COVID-19 because that really helped a lot of companies to go overseas although the companies were here in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And these centres are important one-stop shop that offers our SMEs business advisory, market information and business matching for their global growth.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure him that the Global-Connect@SBF has expanded its service offerings to help our SMEs better navigate the increasingly complex trade environment.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And with the reopening of international borders, we are certainly working hard not just in MTI but across all our economy agencies to spur more of our Singapore enterprises to take the first steps overseas to expand their presence in existing markets so that we can collectively develop a vibrant ecosystem of Singapore enterprises which are future-ready and globally competitive.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
text: Chairman, I thank both the Ministers and both the Ministers of State for their clear speeches.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
text: Indeed, I am encouraged to hear the continued push by MTI for SMEs to digitise.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
text: One is for the Minister of State's clarification on – and their assessment of the successes of the state of digitisation of our SMEs, given that there are very big ones, there are medium ones and there are small ones.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
text: Second clarification for the Minister of State is, if there can be more proactive engagement with smaller SMEs, especially those who are keen to digitise but do not know how or where to, beyond the mere availing of portals as well as SME centres, can there be a more proactive push given that as SMEs do compete with each other too and may not be most keen to help each other in this regard.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Mr Chairman, I want to thank the Member Mr Derrick Goh for his question.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And we agree with him that in MTI and our economic agencies, we take a differentiated approach to support our companies, whether they are micro-enterprises or they are SMEs or larger local companies with the potential to become a Singapore Global Enterprise.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And, for example, if I talk about the 15,000 heartland shops in all our precincts and it is really heartening that during COVID-19, they hunkered down, they worked with us and I want to say a big thank you to TACs like the Federation or Merchants Association Singapore (FMAS) that Mr Desmond Choo talked about and the Heartland Enterprise Centre Singapore (HECs) for working with us.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Because they are very important opinion multipliers and like what Mr Derrick Goh mentioned, they are not only the voice of the companies but they will know the pain points and what are some of the emerging trends and opportunities.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And I touch on TACs because I always say that the TACs play a very important "ABC" role and the Government sees a lot of benefit and value in working closely with a TAC.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And I think the various TAC chiefs will agree with us that in the last three years because we have to work together, bridge the communications to overcome COVID-19, the various series of heightened measures, we have now fostered a very strong working relationship with the TACs.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And the two announcements that I have mentioned, we will strengthen the nexus with SGTech, so that SGTech can also support the other TACs in facilitating and catalysing enterprise digitalisation, not just in a broadbased manner, but actually sectorial and sub-sectorial.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And last year, I cited Heng Foh Tong which is an herbal tea heartland shop.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, we are glad that we have this critical base of companies whether is it heartland shops, SMEs, larger local companies who see the benefits of going digital and now we will continue to work with them to push it further so that they can leverage on technology to scale to global markets.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This is supplemental to Member Derrick Goh's question – SMEs that are currently new to digital technology can adapt or adopt startup digital packs under the SMEs Go Digital programme which helps SMEs to start right with foundational digital tools such as accounting or digital marketing.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The second data point which is quite useful for his understanding is also a programme called Growth Digital, which helps SMEs expand into overseas markets.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We are growing this, we are helping them to digitalise and they are early indicators of success.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Allow me to thank Minister Gan Kim Yong, Minister Tan See Leng, Minister of State Low Yen Ling and Minister of State Alvin Tan for their super comprehensive replies and responses.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I do not believe they come from ChatGPT, the responses.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: But we wish MTI every success in your vision 2030.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, with that, I beg leave to withdraw my amendments.
